Forwarding Finexa's note and attachments. Drafting a concise ownership checklist we can paste into the MAP and into the contract row. My recommendations below — I included pragmatic turnaround SLAs so we don't stall the close.

--- Proposed redline ownership checklist (to put in MAP row):
- Commercial (payment/fees/termination): responsible party = Finexa (Procurement). Redwood point-of-contact: Evelyn Hart. Expected turnaround: Finexa -> Redwood = 5 business days.
- MSA operational clauses (indemnity, liability cap, IP): responsible party = Redwood (Contracts). Redwood turnaround for first counter: 48 business hours.
- DPA & Data processing annex (data flows, subprocessors): responsible party = Redwood (Privacy) for technical replies; Finexa to flag any unacceptable clauses within 72 business hours.
- SLA & Availability: Redwood will propose measurable SLA language and offer fallback model variants; Redwood to respond within 48 business hours. If SLA impacts go-live commitment, tag as 'Critical' and escalate to Vanessa.

--- Communication & versioning rules:
- All edits to be checked in via DocuSign/Drive with versioned filenames (e.g., Finexa_MSA_redlines_vF1.docx).
- Each exchange must include a 1-line summary of the change set (e.g., "Redlined: liability cap; added KMS clause").
- If either party expects >2 substantive redline rounds on a single clause, run a 30-min alignment call and log the decision in the MAP.

I will prepare the "redline-ownership-checklist.pdf" and update Finexa_MAP_v0.3.xlsx with these rows. Can we lock Redwood's internal SLA to 48 hours for first-pass responses? If yes, I'll publish into the MAP and push to Finexa for sign-off.
